newsitem.title: OMAN: Oman signs contract to develop container port.
newsitem.headline: Oman signs contract to develop container port.

text.p: Oman on Wednesday signed a $250 million concession deal with Salalah Port Services Company to develop and manage a transhipment container terminal at the port of Mina Raysut, a Ministry of Communications statement said.
The contract is for the development of four container berths capable of handling more than 1.7 million 20-foot equivalent units (TEUs) of transhipment cargo when completed in 1998.
Oman hopes the new port will establish it as a gateway for container traffic in the Gulf, east Africa and India.
"This will place Mina Raysut amongst the largest ports in the world in this category," the ministry statement said.
Salalah Port Services Company founder shareholders are the Omani government, CSX Corp's Sea-Land Services Inc, local firms and pension funds.
The government is investing $140 million in the project and 20 percent of company shares will be offered for public subscription.

"This agreement relates to the development of four container transhipment berths including dredging the entrance and manoeuvring basin up to 16 metres depth as a first stage," the ministry statement said.
Salalah Ports Services Company will operate the terminal under the concession for 30 years.
Tenders for the work are expected to be issued at the end of October.
Mina Raysut's masterplan calls for the development of more than 10 berths and dry dock facilities.
